slides.0.subtitle: Mistral, drought, irrigation, organics and climate change
slides.1.title: Wind and water
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Mistral
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A cold, dry north wind that dries the vines and lowers disease pressure, but can damage shoots and flowering
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Summer drought
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Mediterranean summers are hot and dry, so water is the main limiting factor; sunshine-hour figures vary by source and are not tested
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Wildfire risk
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Drought plus Mistral makes wildfire a shared threat in Provence and Corsica
slides.1.content: The wind brings health and risk.
slides.2.title: Irrigation and management
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Irrigation
slides.2.highlights.0.content: INAO rules allow conditional irrigation, but irrigated plots carry lower loads (Côtes de Provence 7,000 / 6,500 kg/ha)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Organic
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Many appellations push organics and fewer herbicides; the Les Baux specification bans herbicides
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Variety choice
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Late-ripening, drought-tolerant Mourvèdre, Carignan and Vermentino are valued
slides.2.content: Water management drives quality and consistency.
slides.3.title: Climate change
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Faster ripening
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Warming speeds sugar accumulation and makes acid and phenolic ripeness harder to align
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Higher and cooler sites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Higher sites like Coteaux Varois and Pierrevert gain appeal
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Style pressure
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Keeping rosé pale, fresh and moderate in alcohol gets harder
